readerQuestion: How can I set up Home Assistant's Threshold helper so a sensor produces a steady on/off status, and check the switching points without operating real equipment?
directAnswer: Use a single upper limit for a high status or a single lower limit for a low status, with hysteresis as the distance on each side. Do not fill both limit fields to request on-high/off-low behavior. Rehearse with Number → Template sensor → Threshold, keeping the input visible; missing values and helper recreation do not preserve a trustworthy previous status.
originalContribution: Sections 2–4 derive upper 60/hysteresis 5 for above-65 activation and below-55 clearing, provide a complete UI-compatible harmless test setup, and walk through seven ordered inputs including exact equality and the same value with different prior states. The troubleshooting table distinguishes a missing slider, accidental range mode, retained state, template input failure and an unrelated downstream automation. The exact upstream update method was executed in isolation for the seven rows plus unknown input, recovery within the band and initial state within the band.
limitations: Documentation and Core 2026.10.4 source research, with an isolated calculation check only. No physical humidity sensor, appliance control, full Home Assistant integration, or Home Assistant UI session was tested. The numerical boundaries are illustrative rather than universal indoor-humidity targets. UI labels can differ in other installed releases. Helper calculation being local does not establish a local source device. Generated cover is identified as an illustration.

This is automated editorial proofreading, not a human or expert review.

claimChecks.claim: Threshold offers upper-only, lower-only and range behavior. A high status with different activation and clearing points uses a single upper limit with hysteresis, not both limits.

Upper 60 and hysteresis 5 uses value >65 to turn on and value <55 to turn off. Ordered inputs 54,60,65,66,60,55,54 produce off,off,off,on,on,on,off. Exact equality retains the preceding status. Verified by executing the tagged upstream _update_state method in isolation.

The Core 2026.10.4 UI selector accepts sensor-domain sources, so the Number helper cannot be selected directly. Numeric lower/upper fields do not accept templates or entity IDs. The article supplies a Template sensor bridge and leaves the unused lower field empty.

A missing numeric source value sets is_on to None, producing unknown rather than off. Recreated single-limit helpers initialize off inside the hysteresis band, and recovery from unknown at 60 likewise initializes off. The helper is not a persistent memory mechanism.

A Number helper stores a user-controlled value and supports minimum, maximum, step and box/slider display. The rehearsal changes newly created helpers only, with no device disconnection, appliance command or historical data deletion.

UI Template sensors expose State, unit and Availability under Additional options. The example references its exact Number helper ID, returns a number or none, and uses is_number for availability; state-based templates track the referenced entity.

float(default) returns the chosen fallback when numeric conversion fails. float(none) avoids turning a missing source into zero; the independent availability check prevents presenting it as a valid reading.
Unknown and unavailable are separate nonmeasurement states, not off or healthy. A Threshold result must not be read as an all-clear when its source is missing.

Triggers react at a specific change; saving an automation while a condition already holds does not recreate the transition. Creating a new helper does not change an existing automation's input or control an appliance.
Filter produces a processed numeric reading; Threshold produces an on/off decision. The article links the existing Filter guide for smoothing rather than duplicating that setup.
